title: Replace the spinning watcher in concurrent_fetch tests with a deterministic contention seam
description:
internal/runstate/concurrent_fetch_test.go:69 and :168 each run a bare goroutine:

  for { select { case <-stop: return; default: exec.Command("git","-C",dir,"fetch","--quiet","origin").Run() } }

No sleep, no throttle - git fetch spawned back to back for the whole test, saturating a core and hammering the filesystem. Measured 26.47s and 5.37s, i.e. 32s of internal/runstate's 50.7s. The loops also run 60 and 30 iterations of record-writing, counts that look arbitrary: the FETCH_HEAD regression they guard (tick wdb) reproduces within a handful.

Throttling the loop is a band-aid. What the tests actually want is one fact: ANOTHER WRITER MOVED THE REF BETWEEN MY READ AND MY WRITE. Spraying fetches and hoping to land inside that window is why they need 60 iterations and a spinning core. A seam that performs the competing write at exactly that moment makes the test deterministic, near-instant, and immune to machine load.

This is first in the epic because it is also a cy2 fix: these two tests are a load source that flips OTHER tests in the same run.
acceptance_criteria: The FETCH_HEAD/concurrent-fetch guards provoke their contention deterministically, with no unthrottled loop and no iteration count chosen by feel. Reintroducing the wdb regression still fails them. internal/runstate's wall clock drops by at least 25 seconds, and the package no longer saturates a core while it runs.
